scenes.title: Kafka Streams & ksqlDB
scenes.subtitle: Processing streams inside the Kafka ecosystem
scenes.narration: Kafka Streams and ksqlDB let you transform, aggregate, and join event streams directly, without a separate processing cluster.

scenes.title: Two Ways to Process
bullets: Kafka Streams is a Java library in your app
ksqlDB lets you process streams with SQL
Both support stateful operations and joins
State is backed by compacted changelog topics
scenes.narration: Kafka Streams is a Java library you embed directly in your application, so there is no cluster to manage. ksqlDB layers a SQL interface on top, letting analysts and engineers process streams with familiar queries. Both support stateful operations such as aggregations, windows, and joins. Their state is durably backed by compacted changelog topics in Kafka itself.

scenes.title: Streams vs Tables

left.heading: KStream
points: Each record is an independent event

scenes.narration: A core idea in both tools is the duality between streams and tables. A KStream treats each record as an independent event with append semantics, ideal for facts like clicks or payments. A KTable represents the latest value per key with update semantics, ideal for current state like an account balance. You can convert freely between the two depending on the question you are answering.

scenes.title: Aggregating with ksqlDB
scenes.code:
-- ksqlDB: count orders per user in 1-minute windows
CREATE TABLE orders_per_user AS
  SELECT user_id,
         COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders_stream
  WINDOW TUMBLING (SIZE 1 MINUTE)
  GROUP BY user_id
  EMIT CHANGES;
scenes.narration: This ksqlDB statement builds a continuously updating table from an orders stream. It groups records by user and counts them within tumbling one-minute windows. The EMIT CHANGES clause makes the query run forever, updating results as new events arrive. Under the hood, ksqlDB compiles this SQL into a Kafka Streams topology, giving you scalable stream processing without any Java code.

scenes.text: Reach for Kafka Streams when you want processing embedded in a JVM app; reach for ksqlDB when SQL gets the job done faster and simpler.
scenes.narration: Reach for Kafka Streams when you want processing embedded directly in a JVM application. Reach for ksqlDB when SQL gets the job done faster and more simply.
